transformations.edit: Replaced the seed string recorder with an executable Verus function whose body preserves the Rust 1.96 target shape: `let suffix = suffix_pattern.as_slice(); let (len, n) = (slice.len(), suffix.len()); if n <= len { let (head, tail) = slice.split_at(len - n); if tail == suffix { return Some(head); } } None`, adapted only by naming the receiver parameter `slice` and using a local source-backed SlicePattern trait boundary.

Modeled `suffix.as_slice()` as the target-local `SlicePattern::as_slice` trait method whose postcondition is exactly `slice_pattern_view::<P, T>(suffix_pattern)`, preserving the generated contract vocabulary without assuming the public target.

Modeled the guarded comparison `tail == suffix` as target-local `rust_1_96_tail_eq_suffix`, carrying only the generated suffix relation after split_at establishes that `tail` is the source suffix of length `n`. This records the frozen slice PartialEq / SlicePartialEq::equal_same_length implementation without externalizing the public target.
Kept the body's `slice.split_at(len - n)` call executable and used `Seq::lemma_split_at` only to connect the returned head and tail to the generated remaining-prefix postcondition.

Added the generated `slice_strip_suffix_result`, `slice_pattern_view`, `slice_is_suffix`, and `partial_eq_observed` vocabulary as the Verus ensures clause on the executable target and the narrow source-backed boundaries; this records the contract under test and does not use assume_specification.
